subject: Draft DPA incident-notice language and evidence requests
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme.io>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.io
Date: 2026-12-17T14:03:00-05:00
Subject: Clarify breach notice windows and evidence scope

Avery,

Quick note from Acme legal/security: we are updating our vendor DPA and want to make sure the incident-notice & cooperation section from Redwood aligns with our internal expectations. Two asks:

1) Notice timing: under our DPA we currently require the processor to notify the controller "without undue delay and no later than 48 hours after confirmation of a breach." Can Redwood accept a guaranteed 48-hour window for confirmed incidents, and a 24-hour initial acknowledgement if there is evidence of suspected unauthorized access?

2) Evidence & cooperation: we need specifics on the types of forensic evidence Redwood can provide (logs, timeline, affected tenant IDs, export of audit logs, SOC 2 report excerpts). We will also likely request a brief statement on whether data transfers use SCCs and whether Redwood will assist in any cross-border supervisory authority correspondences.

Can you confirm and propose a short paragraph we can include in the DPA? Also flag any items that require Security/Eng sign-off (forensics, data extracts).

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Senior Counsel, Acme Payments
Elena.Morales@acme.io

--
Attachment: incident-evidence-checklist.xlsx (attachment stub)

From: avery.johnson@redwood.ai <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-17T15:08:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarify breach notice windows and evidence scope

Laura / Dev, FYI — Acme legal pinged me about tightening the DPA incident-notice wording. They specifically want a 48-hour maximum for confirmed breaches and a 24-hour acknowledgement for suspected incidents. They also want a list of evidence items we can supply.

Notes from my side:
- We currently pledge "without undue delay" in our standard DPA (legal), which is intentionally flexible. Moving to a bright-line 48h for confirmed incidents will have operational implications (forensics capacity, SLA for running exports).
- We can reliably provide: timeline of events, affected customer/tenant identifiers, high-level root cause, and filtered audit logs for the time window. Full raw disk images and PII extracts are not something we provide by default; for those we'd require a formal request and possibly a controlled environment or a third-party forensic engagement (cost-recoverable).

Can you draft a concise clause that balances Acme's asks with our operational constraints? Also confirm whether SOC 2 report excerpts and SCC confirmation are ok to share (we have a redacted SOC2 and standard SCCs).

Avery
Product Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai

From: dev.patel@redwood.ai <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-12-18T09:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify breach notice windows and evidence scope

Avery / Laura,

Drafting notes from Security/Infra perspective:

- Detection vs confirmation: we can commit to an acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection of a security event that may impact customer data, and a best-effort timeline for confirmation. For confirmed confidentiality breaches we can commit to providing notice to the Controller within 48 hours after confirmation, but we need to keep the language "confirmation" because some investigations require short delay to avoid tipping off an attacker and to preserve forensic integrity.

- Evidence we can provide without additional approvals (standard response):
  * Indexed audit logs (filtered to tenant scope) for the relevant time window
  * Timeline of observable events and actions taken
  * High-level root-cause analysis and remediation steps
  * SOC 2 Type II report (redacted or summary) and CAIQ responses as attachments

- Items that need extra steps / formal request:
  * Full raw logs or system-level snapshots (requires legal request and may need a controlled transfer)
  * Data extractions that include raw PII (we avoid bulk extracts; will provide pseudonymized or filtered versions where feasible)

Proposed short DPA clause (candidate):
"In the event Redwood becomes aware of an incident involving unauthorized access to Customer Data, Redwood will: (a) acknowledge receipt of the incident to Customer within 24 hours of initial detection; (b) provide Customer with written notice of a confirmed confidentiality breach within 48 hours of confirmation of such breach; (c) provide reasonable cooperation and evidence to assist Customer in fulfilling its regulatory notification obligations, which may include tenant-scoped audit logs, event timelines, remediation steps, redacted SOC 2 report excerpts, and other reasonable forensic evidence. Redwood will not be required to provide full system images or bulk PII exports without a separate, mutually agreed process."

We should also include a sentence about SCCs / cross-border support: "Redwood represents that, where applicable, transfers are protected by SCCs and Redwood will cooperate with Customer in responding to supervisory authority inquiries."

If that looks OK I can route to Legal for final wording.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Security Engineering
dev.patel@redwood.ai

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme.io>, avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-19T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarify breach notice windows and evidence scope

Elena,

Thanks for the clear ask — appreciate the specificity. Redwood can accept the following, subject to the carve-outs noted below and the addition of a standard "forensic cooperation" process in the DPA:

1) Notice windows: Redwood will acknowledge an incident that may affect Customer Data within 24 hours of detection and will provide written notice of a confirmed breach within 48 hours of confirmation.

2) Evidence & cooperation: Redwood will provide reasonable cooperation to assist Customer and its regulators, including tenant-scoped audit logs, a timeline of events, remediation measures taken, and redacted SOC 2 Type II report excerpts. Where additional forensic artifacts are required (full system images, raw PII exports), Redwood will provide them only upon a formal documented request and with appropriate safeguards (narrow scope, secure transfer, and cost-recovery when a third-party forensic vendor is engaged). Redwood will also confirm that data transfers are governed by SCCs where applicable and will assist in responding to supervisory authority inquiries.

We are happy to insert the following DPA paragraph (suggested) into the contract:

"Incident Notification and Cooperation. In the event of an actual or suspected security incident affecting Customer Data, Redwood shall: (i) acknowledge the incident to Customer within 24 hours of initial detection; (ii) provide written notice of any confirmed confidentiality breach within 48 hours of confirmation; (iii) provide reasonable cooperation to Customer and its regulators, including scoped audit logs, event timelines, remediation steps, and redacted SOC 2 report excerpts; and (iv) provide additional forensic artifacts (e.g., system images or raw exports) only upon a documented request and subject to mutually agreed technical and legal safeguards. Redwood represents that cross-border transfers are protected by SCCs where required and will cooperate with Customer in supervisory authority communications as reasonably necessary."

If that language works for Acme please confirm and we will provide the redacted SOC2 and CAIQ via our secure share (attached). If you need faster turnaround on any evidence items, please indicate priority and we can escalate to our incident response team.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
